Box 'Test Sample' with airplane icon -> arrow -> dark red box 'Model' with subtitle '[Any value] - (0, +∞)' and purple sigmoid curve icon -> arrow -> blue box '(0 --- 1)' labeled 'Predicted Value' -> arrow -> vertical red box 'Threshold (e.g. 0.5)' -> splits into two arrows -> light green oval 'Class I' and light purple oval 'Class II'.

recreation_brief: 1. Create a blank PowerPoint slide with white background. 2. Add title 'Effect of Selecting Threshold Value on Model Performance' at top in large bold dark red sans-serif font. 3. Add yellow circle with '21' in top-right corner. 4. Draw a red border around the slide content area. 5. Top-left: create a small table with header 'Predicted as' spanning columns P and N; row headers P and N; cells TP/FP and FN/TN; add vertical 'Actual' label on left. 6. Below it: create second table with same headers; cells 5, 0, 4, 2; add vertical 'Actual' label; draw red circle around the cell containing 5. 7. To the right of the top table: add orange/red box with 'Threshold=0.1'. 8. Center-right: draw flowchart: 'Test Sample' box with airplane icon, arrow to dark red 'Model' box with text '[Any value] - (0, +∞)' below and purple curve icon inside, arrow to blue box '(0 --- 1)' with 'Predicted Value' above, arrow to vertical red box 'Threshold (e.g. 0.5)', then branching arrows to green oval 'Class I' and purple oval 'Class II'. 9. Bottom: draw scatter plot area with red x-axis line, tick marks, labels 0.0, 0.5, 1.0. 10. Scatter approximately 12-15 line-drawing airplane icons across the plot area. 11. Add vertical dashed blue line near x=0.1. 12. Ensure all text matches verbatim.
